title: Status
description: Live orchestrator state. Source of truth for /pipeline --resume. current_phase is pattern-validated, not enum-validated: the enum drifted out of sync with the phases the orchestrator actually writes (0.5-map, 2-constraints, 2.5-design, 3-impl-tripwire, ...) and a stale enum derails runs. Canonical values are whatever /pipeline's checkpoint steps write; the pattern only pins the <phase-number>-<slug> shape.

current_phase.description: Examples: 0-setup, 0.5-map, 0.5-map-complete, 1-ba, 1-ba-open-questions, 1-ba-complete, 1-ba-rework-required, 2-constraints, 2-constraints-complete, 2-review, 2-review-complete, 2.5-design, 2.5-design-owner-decision, 2.5-design-complete, 3-impl, 3-impl-tripwire, 3-impl-tripwire-indeterminate, 3-impl-gate-failed, 3-impl-frontend-gate-failed, 3-impl-live-verify-unverified, 3-impl-complete, 4-review, 4-review-complete, 4-veto-rework-required, 5-archive, 5-archived, halted-error. The <phase>-error family is a SHAPE and not a literal -- commands/pipeline.md writes <phase>-error for whichever phase failed -- so it is deliberately not enumerated above. The list is exactly the literals commands/pipeline.md writes, PLUS halted-error, which pipeline.md writes nowhere yet the pattern above alternates by name and scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs returns true for: deriving this list from pipeline.md alone would delete correct work. This is prose in a file nothing validates status.json against, and it rotted once already (#42, which blessed two phases nobody wrote and omitted six that were); it is kept honest now by tests/test-status-schema-contract.sh, which asserts set equality against pipeline.md in BOTH directions.

ask_text.description: Truncated, secret-redacted task summary, written from a human-pasted /pipeline argument. COMMITTED AND ARCHIVED VERBATIM, so whatever lands here reaches a public tree and stays in history; a fix-forward commit does not remove it. Must not carry copied credential material (API key, Bearer token, OAuth code, password, DSN with inline credentials, .env line). DELIBERATELY NO maxLength: the security-relevant dimension of this field is CONTENT, not length, and a cap would refuse correct work -- see commands/pipeline.md's free-text secret rule, which is where the writer reads it. Nothing validates status.json against this schema; the honorer is the writer, and the after-the-fact detector is the credential-shaped scan in tests/test-status-schema-contract.sh.

risk_tier.description: The depth the run executes at, carried here so every later checkpoint and re-run honors the same one. BA sets it in spec.json and the orchestrator validates it when BA returns, but do NOT read this field as evidence that Phase 1 has finished: commands/pipeline.md gates Phase 0.5's map depth by tier, so a record whose 0.5-map has run already carries a tier at its FIRST 1-ba checkpoint, before BA is dispatched. Absence here means no earlier phase set it, never that the tier is trivial.

panel_roles.description: The Phase 4 panel composition resolved by tier and diff surfaces. Recorded before dispatch so the merge, the rubric, and --resume agree on who was on the panel. design_review is APPENDED TO THIS ARRAY whenever the diff touches a frontend surface, and art_director whenever a visual-contract.json exists for the issue; both also write their own shard, exactly like every other role.

worktree_path.description: OPTIONAL, and preferably OMITTED: no code reads this field from status.json. The Phase 3 worktree path lives in tasks.json, which is where Dev writes it and where the orchestrator, QA and validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs all read it. When present here it is for audit only and MUST be a path RELATIVE to the project root, e.g. .claude/worktrees/42-phase3-20260101-120000 -- never an absolute path, and never a sentence about the path, which is a free-text note in a field typed as a path. WRITER PROHIBITION, and it stays a prohibition rather than becoming a promise: status.json is COMMITTED at .pipeline/<n>/status.json, and nothing rewrites it there, so it must never carry an absolute filesystem path, a command string, or a credential. The archival boundary in knowledge-store.mjs does rewrite absolute paths on the way into knowledge/issue-archive, by value shape and across every artifact -- but that is a backstop for the archive copy and it never touches the committed one, so it retires no obligation stated here. archive-pipeline.mjs does not read this field as an artifact fallback; the Phase 4 sync step is what preserves worktree artifacts.

phase3_qa_test_commit.description: Architectural tier only: SHA of QA's committed failing-test contract, recorded before Dev dispatches.

veto_reason.description: Orchestrator prose: a veto reason IS a sentence, which is why it is unbounded. COMMITTED AND ARCHIVED VERBATIM, so whatever lands here reaches a public tree and stays in history; a fix-forward commit does not remove it. Must not carry copied credential material (API key, Bearer token, OAuth code, password, DSN with inline credentials, .env line). DELIBERATELY NO maxLength: the security-relevant dimension of this field is CONTENT, not length, and a cap would refuse correct work -- see commands/pipeline.md's free-text secret rule, which is where the writer reads it. Nothing validates status.json against this schema; the honorer is the writer, and the after-the-fact detector is the credential-shaped scan in tests/test-status-schema-contract.sh.

error.description: Orchestrator prose, and THE SHARPEST OF THESE FIELDS: the natural content of an error field is COPIED MACHINE OUTPUT -- a failed gh/curl echoing a URL with a token, a DB connection error carrying a DSN, a stack trace. COMMITTED AND ARCHIVED VERBATIM, so whatever lands here reaches a public tree and stays in history; a fix-forward commit does not remove it. Must not carry copied credential material (API key, Bearer token, OAuth code, password, DSN with inline credentials, .env line). DELIBERATELY NO maxLength: the security-relevant dimension of this field is CONTENT, not length, and a cap would refuse correct work -- see commands/pipeline.md's free-text secret rule, which is where the writer reads it. Nothing validates status.json against this schema; the honorer is the writer, and the after-the-fact detector is the credential-shaped scan in tests/test-status-schema-contract.sh.

verdict.description: A TOKEN, not prose: the verdict of the phase this event closes. NOTHING VALIDATES status.json AGAINST THIS SCHEMA -- the file is in no AGENT_RULES entry in scripts/validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs, and that walker does not implement maxLength at all, so this cap refuses nothing on its own. It is honored by the writer and by tests/test-status-schema-contract.sh, which checks every committed record against the value read FROM here. Do not mistake the cap for an enforced control and skip writing the enforcement. The bound exists because status.json is committed AND archived verbatim, so an unbounded string here reaches a public tree at full length; 32 is 1.78x the longest declared verdict (APPROVE_WITH_NOTES, 18) and sits below the length of the sentence this refuses. Optional: an event with no verdict is valid.

note.description: Orchestrator prose, unbounded on purpose: a 600-char note recording a live reproduction is correct work, and #52 ruled that capping it would destroy audit content to solve a problem length was never the mechanism of. COMMITTED AND ARCHIVED VERBATIM, so whatever lands here reaches a public tree and stays in history; a fix-forward commit does not remove it. Must not carry copied credential material (API key, Bearer token, OAuth code, password, DSN with inline credentials, .env line). DELIBERATELY NO maxLength: the security-relevant dimension of this field is CONTENT, not length, and a cap would refuse correct work -- see commands/pipeline.md's free-text secret rule, which is where the writer reads it. Nothing validates status.json against this schema; the honorer is the writer, and the after-the-fact detector is the credential-shaped scan in tests/test-status-schema-contract.sh.

review_rounds.description: How many Phase 4 panel rounds this issue has run (the first full panel is 1; each delta re-review adds 1). An EXPLICIT counter because events[] items carry only phase and at, with no round field, so the count cannot be inferred from them.

telemetry.description: Derived, NUMBERS ONLY. Computed from events[] by scripts/pipeline-telemetry.mjs. No note, no path, no command string: this file is archived verbatim.

phase_elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds spent per phase, keyed by the leading phase LABEL of the event that CLOSED it, resolved through KNOWN_PHASES in scripts/dispatch-model.mjs. events[] entries are EXIT markers -- each carries the `verdict` of the phase it closes, and a verdict is not knowable until that phase has run -- so an interval belongs to the LATER event's phase, not the earlier one. Keys are KNOWN_PHASES tokens and never raw event labels, so an agent-written label can never become a persisted key in this archived file. The token is not always a number: the architectural tier writes 3a and 3b for its two implementation steps, and both are keys here.

total_lead_time_ms.description: Last timed event minus the first. NO `minimum`, deliberately: it is negative when events[] timestamps run backwards, which is a value this repo's own records produce and which the sibling unattributed_ms documents as a supported signal. Forbidding it would be a contract that contradicts its own corpus.

unattributed_ms.description: Milliseconds between events that no phase key could absorb. sum(phase_elapsed_ms) + unattributed_ms == total_lead_time_ms holds by construction, so a phase label this pipeline writes but KNOWN_PHASES does not declare shows up here as a visible number instead of being silently dropped. Negative only when events[] timestamps run backwards, which is itself the signal.

unattributed_events.description: How many event boundaries contributed to unattributed_ms.

untimed_events.description: How many events[] entries were DROPPED before any figure above was computed, because their `at` was unparseable or their `phase` was not a string. Every other number here, total_lead_time_ms INCLUDED, is computed over the surviving events, so the partition balances whether this is 0 or 20 -- a true statement about a population that quietly lost a member. It cannot be folded into unattributed_ms, because an event with no timestamp contributes no duration to attribute, so it is reported as its own count.

review_rounds_observed.description: Panel rounds OBSERVED on phase 4: events labelled 4-review whose verdict is one a panel can return (APPROVE, APPROVE_WITH_NOTES, REQUEST_CHANGES, REQUEST_REFACTOR, VETO). Not every 4-review event is a round -- the corpus also writes delta-dispatch ENTRY markers (delta-dispatched, DELTA) and a `merged` TERMINUS under that same label -- so counting entries overcounts, reporting 4 rounds against 2 real panels on the #43 record. An unrecognized verdict is treated as a marker, which keeps this a floor rather than letting a typo inflate it.

review_rounds_recorded_delta.description: review_rounds minus review_rounds_observed: the hand-maintained counter checked against the events it summarizes. Zero means they agree (and is what an absent counter yields, since review_rounds is then the observation itself). Non-zero means the counter disagrees with the record, signed so the direction survives. On the committed corpus this is non-zero on 5 of 7 records in BOTH directions (+2 on #43, -2 on #56, +1 on #17 and #39 which never entered phase 4 at all); the two it gets right are both single-round runs, so hand-maintenance was reliable exactly where nothing depended on it. Any budget that binds on round count must read this field, not review_rounds alone. No `minimum`: it is negative whenever the counter undercounts.

attribution.description: Which convention the figures above were computed under. Records written by 0.21.0 or earlier carry no attribution and were computed under the entry-marker convention; treat those figures as historical and stale rather than recomputing them. A closed enum, not free text, because this file is archived verbatim.

effective_config.description: The surface globs and per-role models that were LIVE for this run, so a narrowing is auditable after the fact rather than reconstructable only from a config file that may have changed since. The two migration sets are SEPARATE named entries deliberately: the gate's set REPLACES the defaults and the tripwire's UNIONS with them, and an auditor who cannot tell which was live for which control has learned nothing. An absolute-path glob is recorded as the literal token <absolute-glob-rejected>.

flags.description: One-line-per-agent digest appended after each agent returns; Phase 4 reviewers read this instead of re-parsing earlier artifacts from cold.

verdict.description: The same TOKEN-not-prose rule and the same 32-char bound as events[].verdict, and unenforced in exactly the same way: nothing validates status.json against this schema, so the cap is honored by the writer and by tests/test-status-schema-contract.sh rather than by a validator. Capped alongside its twin rather than deferred because it carries the LONGEST verdict in the committed corpus (APPROVE_WITH_NOTES, 18 chars) while events[] tops out at 15. Optional: a flag with no verdict is valid.

summary.description: ALSO unenforced by any validator: this cap predates the two above and is honored only because commands/pipeline.md restates it as a writer rule. The 140 is a DIGEST bound and is not a secret control: this field is COMMITTED AND ARCHIVED VERBATIM like the other free-text fields, and 140 characters is ample room for a token. The secret rule that governs it is the content rule in commands/pipeline.md, not this number.
